headline: Attackers are already walking past SAML multifactor checks on SonicWall SSL-VPN, while agentic AI frameworks reach banks and Claude Code's approval file leaves developer secrets in 1,122 public GitHub repositories.

emerging_trends.text: Microsoft's finding that Storm-3358 points ARTEX at banks and insurers moves agentic attack frameworks out of state espionage and into profit-driven crime, which widens the pool of companies that will meet an automated intruder this quarter.
emerging_trends.topic_title: ARTEX Abuse Reaches the Financial Sector

emerging_trends.text: Apiiro counted 1,122 public repositories holding secrets that Claude Code wrote into its settings file, and BlueFlag Security reports that 99% of repository access tokens never expire, so one careless approval hands an attacker credentials that outlive the project.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Claude Code Approvals Leak Keys to GitHub

emerging_trends.text: Five United States federal agencies, Unit 42, and Wired converged this week on the same point: cheap internet-connected refrigeration controllers now sit inside the supply chains of grocers and blood banks, and the operators running them rarely alarm on a setpoint change.

topics.title: Unit 42 Dissects Europe's Refrigeration Attacks
topics.latest_developments: Wired called the spree an internet-of-things wake-up call on November 7, 2026, pinning the damage at blood labs and grocery stores on basic security lapses in internet-connected devices, a day after Unit 42, the Palo Alto Networks research group, published its own examination with defense and mitigation steps, SecurityWeek detailed the call from CISA, the FBI, Health and Human Services, the Department of Agriculture, and the Department of Transportation for operators to harden refrigeration controllers, and Dark Reading traced the speed of the spread to shared controller platforms across the grocery industry.
topics.summary: Intruders reached cooling systems at supermarkets in Belgium, Sweden, Ireland, Estonia, and Luxembourg and at three sites of the Établissement français du sang, the French civilian blood service, switching evaporators into defrost and heating cycles that spoiled stock and risked equipment damage and fire. Operators should segment controller networks, close remote management to the internet, and alarm on temperature setpoint changes.

sources.title: Turning Up the Heat: Inside the Attacks on Europe's Refrigeration System
The Fridge-Hacking Spree Is an Internet-of-Things Wake-Up Call
US Agencies Urge Organizations to Harden Refrigeration Controllers
Why Europe's Freezer Hacks Spread So Far, So Fast

topics.title: SonicWall SSL-VPN Flaw Defeats SAML Logins
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer spelled out the mechanism on November 7, 2026: CVE-2026-19868 lets an attacker who already holds credentials for one login method walk past SAML checks on SonicOS SSL-VPN, SAML-enforced multifactor authentication included, and attackers are using it now.
topics.summary: SonicWall shipped updates for seven SonicOS firewall flaws, the exploited authentication bypass among them, and CISA placed that bug in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Administrators running SonicOS firewalls with SSL-VPN should install the new firmware and rotate VPN credentials.

sources.title: SonicWall Patches Exploited SonicOS Vulnerability That Weakens VPN Logins
SonicWall warns of new SSL-VPN MFA bypass flaw exploited in attacks
CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog

topics.title: Gift Card and Rental Scams Work the Holidays
topics.latest_developments: CTM360 detailed on November 7, 2026 how scammers impersonate major brands and celebrities to run fake gift card giveaways that harvest personal information and sign victims up for unwanted subscriptions, moving the money through affiliate networks, while Fortra's Intelligence and Research Experts team spotted and took down copies of holiday rental platforms that staff a live chat window to talk hesitant travelers into handing over passwords and card numbers.
topics.summary: Both campaigns copy the branding, listings, ratings, and reviews of real consumer platforms, then add a verification step or an urgent message to rush the visitor. Employers should warn staff ahead of holiday travel booking and tell them to reach rental and retail sites through a typed address rather than a search ad or message link.

sources.title: CTM360 Exposes Fake Gift Card Scams Exploiting Trusted Brands
Rental phishing sites use live chat to win over hesitant travelers

topics.title: ARTEX Abuse Reaches the Financial Sector
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported late on November 6, 2026 that Storm-3358, a financially motivated actor, began aiming the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX at financial sector organizations in October 2026, which moves the tool out of the espionage column that CrowdStrike's Vapor Panda attribution had defined.
topics.summary: ARTEX is an open-source multi-agent penetration-testing framework whose operators automate reconnaissance, exploitation, and the work that follows a break-in, including scraping GitHub for OAuth application secrets to take authenticated actions inside victims' cloud tenants. Banks and insurers should hunt their public code for live application secrets and audit third-party application consent inside their identity platforms.

sources.title: ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector

topics.title: Claude Code Approvals Leak Keys to GitHub
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News reported on November 7, 2026 that the software security company Apiiro found passwords and API keys sitting in 1,122 public GitHub repositories, put there by Claude Code when developers approved a command with the do-not-ask-again option.
topics.summary: Anthropic's coding assistant saves an approved command word for word in a project settings file, secret included, and developers then commit that file to source control where anyone can read it. Teams should rotate every credential ever typed into a Claude Code command and strip the settings file from their repositories and history.

sources.title: Claude Code's “Don't Ask Again” File Exposes Passwords and Keys in 1,122 Public Copies on GitHub

topics.title: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Heist Runs Through a Supplier
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer reported on November 7, 2026 that the fraudulent transactions at Crédit Mutuel Arkéa reached as much as $133 million and that the French cooperative bank suspended certain systems in response, the first account of operational shutdown since the bank's November 4, 2026 press notice naming a compromised service provider as the entry point.
topics.summary: Attackers broke into one of the bank's suppliers, which the bank still leaves unnamed, then moved money out of Crédit Mutuel Arkéa's own account. Banks should inventory every supplier that can initiate or approve payment instructions and require out-of-band confirmation above a transfer threshold.

sources.title: Hackers pull off $133 million French bank heist via service provider

topics.title: Vendors Mine Security Records for Model Training
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading reported on November 6, 2026 that security vendors increasingly feed their customers' incident records into model training, and a Vanson Bourne survey of 3,600 business decision-makers published the same day found that 87% want a better way to approve, monitor, and control AI use while more than half said the AI their teams run already acts inside defined rules with no routine review.
topics.summary: An incident archive holds the mapped weaknesses, credentials, and response gaps of the company that generated it, and training a shared model on that record carries the exposure outward. Security leaders should read the data-use clauses in their detection and response contracts and set an approval path for autonomous AI before the tools outrun the policy.

sources.title: AI Gave Your Incident Archive a Second Job
87% say their AI controls need to work better

topics.title: Ransomware Crews Ride Hypervisor Misconfiguration
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky's Securelist published a breakdown on November 6, 2026 of ransomware cases on VMware ESXi and Proxmox hosts, mapping the attack layers of a virtual environment and the specific misconfigurations that turn one hypervisor compromise into the encryption of every guest it runs.
topics.summary: A hypervisor parks dozens of production servers behind a single management interface, so an exposed or weakly separated ESXi or Proxmox console converts one stolen credential into datacenter-wide encryption. Administrators should pull hypervisor management off routable networks, enforce multifactor authentication on it, and keep backups outside the virtual environment.

sources.title: Virtualization security: attack layers and misconfiguration impact

topics.title: Perry Johnson Subsidiaries Settle With Four States
topics.latest_developments: The attorneys general of Connecticut, New Jersey, New York, and Michigan settled on November 6, 2026 with the medical transcription, coding, and imaging subsidiaries of Perry Johnson Companies, the Nevada-based parent, over a 2023 hack that exposed sensitive patient records.
topics.summary: The subsidiaries process dictation, billing codes, and medical images for hospitals and physician practices, which parks patient records in a vendor far from the doctor who collected them. Health systems should map which business associates hold their patient data and check what each one owes them after a breach.

sources.title: Medical services company settles with 4 states over 2023 hack of sensitive patient records

business_politics.title: Eisenkot Gets First Try at an Israeli Government
business_politics.latest_developments: Israeli President Isaac Herzog handed opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government Saturday, November 7, starting a 28-day clock.
business_politics.summary: Eisenkot, a former chief of the general staff of the Israel Defense Forces, must now assemble a coalition that would unseat Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, and he does it while Washington weighs renewed strikes on Iran.

sources.title: Israel’s president gives Gadi Eisenkot first chance at forming a government
Netanyahu’s Challenger Tapped to Try to Form Israeli Government

business_politics.title: Hegseth Digs In Against Impeachment
business_politics.latest_developments: The Wall Street Journal reported Saturday, November 7, that Hegseth has mounted an aggressive campaign to fight the impeachment vote set for next week.
business_politics.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faces a congressional vote on his impeachment next week and has refused to step back, and critics in Congress warn that a defiant Pentagon chief could put military funding at risk.

sources.title: With a vote on his impeachment looming next week, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is digging in his heels

business_politics.title: U.S. Intelligence Links Huang to an Alleged Chinese Spy
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Saturday, November 7, that American intelligence officials warned Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang he had carried on a romantic relationship with an executive whom China recruited to gather information on the company.
business_politics.summary: Nvidia sits at the center of the artificial-intelligence build-out and of Washington's export controls on Beijing, and the warning drops its chief executive's personal conduct into that national-security fight.

sources.title: US believes Nvidia’s Huang had romantic relationship with alleged Chinese spy

business_politics.title: Europe Traces Mass Bomb Hoaxes Toward Russia
business_politics.latest_developments: European security agencies now work from the hypothesis that pro-Kremlin activists or hacking groups produced the coordinated threats, the Financial Times reported Saturday, November 7.
business_politics.summary: A wave of bomb threats and hacks hit Europe this week, diverting dozens of flights and forcing media outlets to evacuate, and authorities across several countries still cannot name who sent them.

sources.title: European security agencies probe whether bomb hoaxes started in Russia
Someone Is Causing Chaos Across Europe. The Question Is: Who?

business.title: Sewage Backup Closes Big Shot Bob's in Penn Hills
business.latest_developments: Allegheny County health officials shut the Penn Hills wing restaurant Saturday, November 7, after sewage backed up inside it.
business.summary: Big Shot Bob's, the wing shop in Penn Hills, Allegheny County, stopped serving when county health inspectors ordered it closed over the sewage backup.

sources.title: Penn Hills' wing restaurant closed due to sewage backup

business.title: Allegheny County Will Require Designated Paid Sick Days
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Saturday, November 7, that a new Allegheny County policy will require employers to provide designated paid sick days, a change to the county's existing sick leave rules that moved through with little public debate.
business.summary: Allegheny County drew heavy attention for its 12-week paid parental leave mandate, and alongside it the county rewrote its paid sick leave requirements, obliging employers to set aside specific paid sick days for workers.

sources.title: New Allegheny County policy would require employers to provide designated paid sick days

business.title: Questions Follow the Paid Parental Leave Law
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Saturday, November 7, that Allegheny County's paid parental leave law now faces open questions about its rollout.
business.summary: Allegheny County passed legislation in October 2026 requiring employers to provide paid parental leave, the first mandate of its kind for the county, and employers and advocates want to know how the county will put it into effect.

sources.title: Allegheny County’s paid parental leave law faces questions over rollout

business.title: A Westmoreland Nursing Home Search Shows the Squeeze
business.latest_developments: TribLive published the Steffey family's search Saturday, November 7, as a measure of how little long-term care capacity Pennsylvania has left.
business.summary: Brigid and Al Steffey Sr. of Westmoreland County hunted for a nursing home bed knowing time ran against them, and their search traces the staffing and capacity shortage running through Pennsylvania's long-term care industry.

sources.title: Westmoreland family’s nursing home search highlights Pa. care crisis

around_town.title: The Veterans Day Parade Fills Downtown
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh's Veterans Day parade stepped off Saturday morning, November 7, and drew crowds along the downtown route.
around_town.summary: The parade, which Pittsburgh counts among the largest and longest-running in the United States, honored veterans through downtown streets; TribLive found Patricia Blazewick waiting at the curb with an American flag in each red-gloved hand.

sources.title: American heroes honored at Pittsburgh Veterans Day Parade
‘Honoring those who served’: Crowds gather for Pittsburgh’s annual Veterans Day parade

around_town.title: A Breezy Sunday After Lows in the 30s
around_town.latest_developments: Scattered light showers crossed the Pittsburgh area Saturday evening, November 7, and overnight lows fall into the 30s.
around_town.summary: WPXI's evening forecast carries clouds, chill, and spotty light showers into the night, and WTAE turns Sunday more seasonal and breezy across Western Pennsylvania, with the wind holding up through Monday.

sources.title: Light showers Saturday evening before lows drop to the 30s overnight
Pittsburgh: More seasonal, still breezy for Sunday

around_town.title: Pittsburgh Regional Transit Plans a Carnegie Station Rebuild
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Regional Transit will hold a virtual meeting on the project, WPXI reported Saturday, November 7.
around_town.summary: Carnegie Station sits at the terminus of the West Busway in Carnegie borough, and Pittsburgh Regional Transit wants to modernize the existing transit facility there.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Regional Transit to host virtual meeting about planned Carnegie Station improvements

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Courts Move on AI Citations
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Saturday, November 7, that Pennsylvania may require lawyers and other court filers to verify citations that artificial intelligence generates.
around_town.summary: Judges across the country have caught filings built on fabricated case citations, and Pennsylvania's court system is now weighing a rule putting the burden of verification on the lawyers and self-represented parties who file them.

sources.title: Pennsylvania may require lawyers, other court filers to verify AI-generated citations

around_town.title: The Bell-to-Bell Phone Ban Rests on Districts
around_town.latest_developments: Experts told the Post-Gazette in a story published Saturday, November 7, that the outcome of Pennsylvania's bell-to-bell school cellphone ban depends entirely on how districts carry it out.
around_town.summary: Pennsylvania schools must keep student phones away from bell to bell, and the researchers and educators the Post-Gazette interviewed say enforcement, storage, and exceptions will decide whether the policy changes anything in classrooms.

sources.title: How Pennsylvania's bell-to-bell phone ban pans out depends on implementation, experts say

events.title: 'The Pitt' Must Answer the 'ER' Lawsuit
events.latest_developments: A judge has allowed the suit to go forward, the Post-Gazette reported Friday, November 6.
events.summary: The lawsuit claims that "The Pitt," the hospital drama set and filmed in Pittsburgh, amounts to an unauthorized reboot of "ER," and the case now proceeds past the stage where the show's side sought dismissal.

sources.title: Lawsuit claiming 'The Pitt' is an unauthorized reboot of 'ER' allowed to go forward

events.title: A Thomas Jefferson Percussionist Goes Viral With 'Thunderstruck'
events.latest_developments: WTAE spoke with the student Saturday, November 7, who said the scale of the attention stunned them.
events.summary: A Thomas Jefferson High School senior played AC/DC's "Thunderstruck" on mallet percussion with the marching band, and video of the performance has drawn millions of views.

sources.title: Thomas Jefferson band member stunned as 'Thunderstruck' performance goes viral
‘Mom, I’m going viral again’: Millions are ‘Thunderstruck’ by Thomas Jefferson marching band performance

around_teams.title: Jack Ham Hospitalized Before Penn State's Game
around_teams.latest_developments: Jack Ham went to a hospital Saturday, November 7, after a medical emergency ahead of Penn State's game at Washington.
around_teams.summary: Ham, 77, the Hall of Fame linebacker who played his entire career with the Steelers and now works as an analyst on Penn State football radio broadcasts, fell ill before the Nittany Lions kicked off.

sources.title: Steelers Hall of Fame linebacker Jack Ham hospitalized ahead of Penn State-Washington game

team_usa.title: Kansas City Ends Angel City's Season on a Penalty
team_usa.latest_developments: The Kansas City Current beat Angel City FC in a National Women's Soccer League quarterfinal Saturday, November 7, on a penalty kick that Angel City interim head coach Leif Smerud called "tremendously cheap."
team_usa.summary: Angel City, the Los Angeles club that signed United States under-17 forward Maddie DiMaria this week, goes out of the playoffs, and Kansas City advances toward the NWSL Championship.

sources.title: Angel City slam 'tremendously cheap' penalty in Current quarterfinal win

team_usa.title: Reyna Leaves Hurt Before Nations League Camp
team_usa.latest_developments: U.S. Soccer announced Saturday, November 7, that Gio Reyna will miss the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal with an unspecified injury, hours after he scored and exited Strasbourg's loss.
team_usa.summary: Reyna had regained fitness and form at Strasbourg after years of injuries, and his withdrawal costs coach Mauricio Pochettino a second player in the Haiti window, following defender George Campbell, whom Mark McKenzie replaced.

sources.title: Reyna scores, exits with apparent injury ahead of USMNT camp
USMNT's Reyna to miss Nations League quarterfinals with injury
